## Cloud credentials and API URL

`--api-key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work before or aft
er descendants (`mcpjam cloud --api-key sk_… eval list` and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). Local commands,
including hosted `readiness`, reject those flags at the program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-key`.\n\nCredent

ial precedence for Cloud commands:

1. `--api-key` — must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.
2. `MCPJAM
_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use it.\n3
. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Missing — Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpja

m cloud status` reports `missing` instead)

API URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (th
e same server without `/api/v1`)\n3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved
before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with

exit `3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`

Every command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads resu
lts) decides its server when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL
` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the tw
o variables naming different servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not
a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command ex
its `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON re
port, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credential
s are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Usi
ng MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` red

acts API keys.

## Cloud project scope

Most Cloud commands pick one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `

project` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`
5. Automatic — the most r
ecently updated project you can see\n\nEmpty `--project` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** se

lect a Cloud CLI project (it is SDK eval reporting only).

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam cloud login
mcpj
am cloud link # writes .mcpjam/project.json (no secrets)\nmcpjam cloud status # zero-network: cred

ential, deployment, selector
mcpjam cloud eval list # uses the link
mcpjam cloud link --remove
```

`mcpjam cloud
eval` run-inspection commands (`status`, `cancel`, `judge`, `iterations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `vid
eo`) follow the same rule — `--project` is optional. `mcpjam cloud sessions list` does too; `--all-projects` restores a cross-proj

ect listing and cannot be combined with `--project`. Hosted `readiness` never reads the project link.

## What `--host` means
\

n`--host` is not one flag. The meaning depends on the command:

| Where | What it selects |
| - | - |
| `server`, `tools`, `re
sources`, `prompts` | An **AI client** (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `cursor`, …). The CLI sends that host's `clientInfo`, capabilities, a
nd protocol version in `initialize`. |\n| `test --host` | One host **template** to emulate for a local suite run: its handshake, t
ool visibility and model settings. Never the real client. |\n| `compat --host` | Which AI clients to report. Repeatable; default i
s all. |\n| `cloud eval --host`, `cloud goals`, `cloud studies` | A **saved project Host** (`<id-or-name>`), the client config an
